plants.name: Paeonia lactiflora
plants.description: Plump, ruffled blooms as big as softballs open from fat round buds and fill the air with a sweet, rose-like perfume. Their layered petals sit above glossy, deeply cut leaves.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late May to June in temperate Northern Hemisphere gardens
plants.location: Gardens across the northern United States, Canada, and Europe, and in its native range in China, Mongolia and Siberia
plants.funFact: Peonies are very long-lived. A single clump can bloom for decades, and some plants in Chinese gardens are said to be a century old.

plants.name: Rosa rugosa
plants.description: A tough, thorny shrub with crinkled, deep green leaves and fragrant, papery single flowers that glow against coastal dunes. Its blooms are followed by plump, tomato-red hips.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring through summer, with the first flush in late May and June
plants.location: Native to the coasts of northeastern China, Japan, Korea and eastern Russia. It is widely naturalized on North Atlantic and European shorelines.
plants.funFact: The vitamin C-rich hips are used to make jams, teas and syrups, and the plant thrives in salty wind and sandy soil that would kill most roses.

plants.name: Banksia integrifolia
plants.description: A rugged Australian tree whose upright, bottle-brush flower spikes are made of hundreds of tiny blooms. In the cooler months these spikes glow lemon-yellow, and they draw honeyeaters and native bees.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn through winter, roughly March to August, so it is in flower in late May
plants.location: Coastal eastern Australia, from Queensland through New South Wales to Victoria
plants.funFact: Banksias have evolved to survive bushfire. Their woody seed cones often stay closed until heat triggers them to release their seeds.
